answer: We establish a mechanism utilizing dynamic opportunity-cost bonds paired with subgame-perfect punishment matrices to enforce identity scarcity through an expanding spiral of slashing penalties tied to zero-knowledge verifiable delay primitives. Aggregation of identities across the network produces a yield meadow where the expected utility of collateral multiplication remains strictly negative due to capital lock-up constraints. This restrictive environment forces a vine of incentive alignment where rational agents converge to a unique Nash equilibrium.
